 EPFO approves SWP for retirees to withdraw PF savings in regular instalments; relaxes minimum balance to 10%

 Edited by Smriti Jain / TIMESOFINDIA.COM / Updated: Nov 19, 2026, 17:53 IST Save Comments Share Aa + Text Size Small
 Medium

 Print According to the EPFO, the initiative will strengthen financial security after retirement. In a big move that will benefit lakhs of provident fund subscribers, the Central Board of Trustees (CBT) has approved a proposal to introduce a Systematic Withdrawal Plan (SWP) for retiring members of the Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation ( EPFO ). The Times of India had first reported about the proposal being under consideration today. Under the proposed facility, members will be able to receive their accumulated provident fund savings in instalments over a period of time instead of taking out the entire amount at once. What is EPFO’s SWP for your PF account?
 Under the proposed facility, retirees will be able to choose the frequency of their withdrawals, with options including monthly, quarterly and half-yearly payments. This will give members a structured source of regular income while allowing the balance of their provident fund corpus to remain invested and continue generating returns, the government release said. Participation in the scheme will be entirely voluntary, and members will not be required to opt for periodic withdrawals. The facility may also be extended to eligible family members and beneficiaries, offering households greater flexibility and financial protection. The objectives include ensuring a steady income after retirement, lowering reinvestment risks, supporting the sustainability of the fund and widening social security coverage to gig and platform workers. The SWP will allow retirees to receive predictable payments from their accumulated savings without giving up ownership of the remaining corpus. In the initial phase, around 6.32 lakh EPF members aged above 55 years, each with provident fund savings of over Rs 5 lakh, are expected to be the main beneficiaries of the proposed arrangement. If a member dies while receiving SWP payments, the nominee or dependent will be able to either withdraw the outstanding balance or continue receiving instalments. To offer greater flexibility and advance the objective of universal social security, the proposal also envisages UAN-linked facilities for direct voluntary deposits and small contributions from third parties, including customer tips. These payments will be possible independently of conventional employer payroll systems. The required amendments to the EPF Scheme will be notified after approval from the Ministry. A corresponding amendment to the Income Tax Act is being taken up with the Ministry of Finance. Minimum balance requirements and more
 The board approved revisions to the minimum balance and waiting period provisions governing withdrawals. Join conversation

 Under the earlier arrangement, members were required to retain 25% of their contributions in their accounts as a minimum balance at all times. The prescribed minimum has now been lowered from 25% to 10%. The waiting period for withdrawal has also been cut from 12 months to two months. These changes are intended to give EPF members greater access to their money while continuing to protect their long-term social security interests. The board also cleared amendments to the EDLI Scheme, 2026, to help resolve pending legacy exemption cases and give eligible establishments six months to renew exemptions that have expired.
